name: Bermuda
note: Britain's oldest remaining overseas territory, settled 1609. A major offshore financial and reinsurance hub; self-governing since 1968 with the UK retaining defense and foreign affairs.

name: Cayman Islands
note: One of the world's largest offshore financial centers, with no direct taxation. Never had a sizeable indigenous population; settled largely by shipwreck survivors and turtle fishermen.

name: British Virgin Islands
note: Uses the US dollar despite being British. A leading jurisdiction for offshore company incorporation.

name: Turks and Caicos Islands
note: Briefly a Canadian province proposal target multiple times over the 20th century; none succeeded.

name: Anguilla
note: Seceded from a joint statehood with Saint Kitts and Nevis in 1967 specifically to remain British.

name: Montserrat
note: Two-thirds of the island, including the former capital Plymouth, has been an exclusion zone since the Soufrière Hills volcano erupted in 1995.

name: Falkland Islands
note: Subject of the 1982 war with Argentina, which still claims the islands as the Islas Malvinas. Sheep farming and fishing licenses dominate the economy.

name: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
note: No permanent civilian population; former whaling stations now abandoned. Also claimed by Argentina.

name: Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha
note: Napoleon's final place of exile and death. Tristan da Cunha, part of the same territory, is the most remote inhabited archipelago on Earth.

name: Gibraltar
note: Ceded by Spain in 1713; sits at the mouth of the Mediterranean. Spain continues to press sovereignty claims and border disputes persist.

name: Pitcairn Islands
note: The least populous jurisdiction in the world, settled by HMS Bounty mutineers and their Tahitian companions in 1790.

name: British Indian Ocean Territory
note: Chagossian population was forcibly removed 1968–1973 to build a US military base on Diego Garcia. The UK agreed in 2024 to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Archipelago to Mauritius while retaining the base.

name: British Antarctic Territory
note: Claimed sector overlaps with Argentine and Chilean claims. Sovereignty over any Antarctic territory is frozen under the Antarctic Treaty.

name: Akrotiri and Dhekelia
note: Two Sovereign Base Areas retained on Cyprus after 1960 independence, hosting RAF and army installations.

name: Isle of Man
note: Not part of the UK; a self-governing Crown Dependency with its own parliament, the Tynwald, claimed as the world's oldest continuous legislature.

name: Jersey
note: Largest of the Channel Islands; a major offshore finance center closer to the French coast than to Britain.

name: Guernsey
note: A bailiwick that also administers Alderney and Sark, the latter still governed under a form of feudal law until 2008.

name: French Guiana
note: Legally as much a part of France as Paris; hosts the Guiana Space Centre, Europe's primary spaceport, chosen partly for its near-equatorial latitude.

name: Guadeloupe
note: An archipelago shaped like a butterfly, split by a narrow mangrove channel between its two main wings.

name: Martinique
note: Mount Pelée's 1902 eruption destroyed Saint-Pierre and killed nearly 30,000 people in minutes, one of the deadliest eruptions of the 20th century.

name: Réunion
note: Home to Piton de la Fournaise, one of the most active shield volcanoes on Earth, and gave its name to the coffee variety Bourbon.

name: Mayotte
note: Voted to remain French in 1974 and 1976 while the rest of the Comoro Islands became independent; the Comoros still claims it.

name: French Polynesia
note: Includes Tahiti, Bora Bora, and the Moruroa atoll, site of French nuclear testing between 1966 and 1996.

name: New Caledonia
note: Holds roughly a quarter of the world's known nickel reserves; independence referendums in 2018–2021 all favored staying French, though turnout in the last was contested.

name: Saint Barthélemy
note: Sold to Sweden in 1784, bought back by France in 1878; the only French Caribbean island with no minimum wage tax on high incomes, a legacy of its free-port history.

name: Saint Martin (French part)
note: Shares one small island with Dutch Sint Maarten under an open, unfenced border in place since 1648.

name: Saint Pierre and Miquelon
note: France's last remaining territory in North America, just off Newfoundland — a fragment of the old colony of New France.

name: Wallis and Futuna
note: Still governed alongside three traditional monarchs (kings of Uvea, Sigave, and Alo) whose authority France formally recognizes.

name: French Southern and Antarctic Lands
note: A scattered set of sub-Antarctic islands (Kerguelen, Crozet, Amsterdam) plus a slice of Antarctica (Adélie Land), used mainly for scientific research.

name: Clipperton Island
note: An uninhabited coral atoll far off Mexico's coast, administered directly by the French government with no local population or council.

name: Aruba
note: Seceded from the Netherlands Antilles in 1986 as a distinct constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

name: Curaçao
note: Willemstad's colorful waterfront, the Handelskade, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site; the island became a separate country in 2010 when the Netherlands Antilles dissolved.

name: Sint Maarten
note: Shares its island with French Saint-Martin; its airport approach over Maho Beach is famous for low-altitude jet landings.

name: Bonaire
note: Unlike Aruba and Curaçao, Bonaire opted to become a special municipality directly part of the Netherlands proper rather than a separate country.

name: Sint Eustatius
note: Was the first foreign port to salute the flag of the newly independent United States in 1776, an event that nearly triggered a war with Britain.

name: Saba
note: A single dormant volcano rising steeply from the sea; its tiny airport runway is among the shortest used by commercial aircraft anywhere.

name: Puerto Rico
note: Residents are US citizens but cannot vote in presidential elections and have no voting members of Congress. Statehood referendums have been held repeatedly without resolution.

name: Guam
note: Home to major US Air Force and Navy bases central to American strategy in the Pacific; residents are US citizens without a voting member of Congress.

name: US Virgin Islands
note: Purchased from Denmark in 1917 for $25 million, largely to keep the naval approaches to the Panama Canal out of German hands during WWI.

name: American Samoa
note: Unlike other US territories, people born here are US nationals but not automatically US citizens at birth.

name: Northern Mariana Islands
note: Voted to become a US commonwealth in the 1970s rather than join independent Guam or the Federated States of Micronesia.

name: United States Minor Outlying Islands
note: A grouped designation for scattered, mostly uninhabited islands including Wake, Midway, Johnston, and Baker/Howland — several disputed as guano-era claims.

name: Greenland
note: The world's largest island; holds broad home rule since 2009 and could become independent by referendum, a prospect drawing renewed US interest in recent years.

name: Faroe Islands
note: Self-governing since 1948 and outside the EU even though Denmark is a member; salmon farming and fishing dominate the economy.

name: Svalbard
note: Governed under the 1920 Svalbard Treaty, which lets other signatory nations' citizens live and work there visa-free; home to the Global Seed Vault.

name: Jan Mayen
note: A volcanic island with no permanent civilian residents, staffed only by meteorological and military personnel.

name: Bouvet Island
note: Widely cited as the most remote island on Earth, over 1,600 km from the nearest land; an uninhabited nature reserve.

name: Peter I Island
note: An ice-covered volcanic island off Antarctica, visited so rarely that it was first landed on only in 1929.

name: Queen Maud Land
note: Norway's Antarctic claim, like all others, is held in abeyance under the Antarctic Treaty System and not internationally exercised as sovereignty.

name: Cook Islands
note: Self-governing in free association with New Zealand since 1965; conducts its own foreign relations and has been admitted to some UN bodies.

name: Niue
note: One of the world's largest coral islands by land area relative to its tiny population; among the least-visited countries/territories on Earth.

name: Tokelau
note: Rejected independence in referendums in 2006 and 2007, both falling just short of the required two-thirds majority.

name: Ross Dependency
note: New Zealand's Antarctic claim, home to Scott Base beside the American McMurdo Station.

name: Norfolk Island
note: Settled by descendants of the Bounty mutineers relocated from overcrowded Pitcairn in 1856; lost most of its self-governing autonomy in 2015.

name: Christmas Island
note: Famous for the annual mass migration of tens of millions of red land crabs across the island to the sea to breed.

name: Cocos (Keeling) Islands
note: A ring of coral atolls governed by the Clunies-Ross family as a private fiefdom for over a century before Australia formally annexed them in 1955.

name: Ashmore and Cartier Islands
note: Uninhabited reef islands important mainly for marking Australia's maritime boundary and exclusive economic zone with Indonesia.

name: Australian Antarctic Territory
note: The largest of all Antarctic territorial claims by area, covering nearly 42% of the continent; recognized by few other states.

name: Coral Sea Islands
note: A scatter of small reefs and islets, mostly a nature reserve, with a single staffed automatic weather station on Willis Island.

name: Heard Island and McDonald Islands
note: One of the few places on Earth with active volcanoes and glaciers together; so remote it's rarely visited even by researchers.

name: Jervis Bay Territory
note: Carved out to give the landlocked Australian Capital Territory a naval outlet to the sea; administered under ACT law rather than any state's.

name: Hong Kong
note: Returned by Britain in 1997 under a 'one country, two systems' framework guaranteeing a separate legal and economic system until at least 2047.

name: Macau
note: Returned by Portugal in 1999 under the same 'one country, two systems' model; now the world's largest gambling market by revenue, well ahead of Las Vegas.

name: Åland Islands
note: Swedish-speaking and demilitarized under international treaties dating to 1856; Finland's only officially monolingual autonomous region.

name: Ceuta
note: A Spanish enclave on the Moroccan coast, giving Spain the EU's only land border with Africa; Morocco continues to claim it.

name: Melilla
note: Spain's other North African enclave, fortified with a heavily monitored border fence to control migration into the EU.
